Mortgage rates could reach 9% in a severe scenario involving a sharp rise in Treasury yields, according to Cotality chief economist Selma Hepp.

The 30-year fixed mortgage rate had reached 7.5% on Tuesday, according to Mortgage News Daily, as Hepp discussed the outlook for mortgage rates during an interview on CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street.”

9% Is Not Base Case

Hepp said a 9% mortgage rate is possible if Treasury yields climb toward 6%-7%, but stressed that "it’s really not our base case scenario."

Such a move would require a severe combination of disruptions, including a debt-limit standoff, a more serious shock to confidence in the Treasury market and further deterioration in the dollar’s safe-haven status.

A temporary spike in Treasury yields combined with a mortgage spread of around 200 basis points could push mortgage rates toward 9%, she said.

But Hepp expects rates to remain closer to current levels. She said the housing market is increasingly being driven by the bond market rather than the Federal Reserve because mortgages are priced off longer-term Treasury yields.

"The most important story in the housing today is no longer Fed. It’s really the bond market," Hepp said.

With bonds in the upper-mid to upper-4% range and mortgage spreads around 200 basis points, she expects mortgage rates to remain around 7% for some time. "I think we’re going to stay there for a little while," she said.

Housing Market Stays Constrained

Hepp said U.S. home sales are currently around 4.7 million, roughly the level seen before the pandemic. Lower rates could support more activity, but affordability remains a major constraint.

Homebuilders have responded with rate buy-downs, seller concessions and products aimed at lower-income households, she said.

Existing homeowners face a different problem. Many are reluctant to move because higher prevailing mortgage rates make their current loans more valuable to keep. Hepp said the wide gap between outstanding mortgage rates and current rates is keeping the existing-home market stuck and turnover very low.

Mortgage purchase applications were recently reported at their lowest level since 1995, while typical monthly mortgage payments, including taxes and insurance, were at about $2,800.

Another recent housing-market assessment found activity was trending toward levels seen in 2023, when about 4 million housing units traded, as higher mortgage rates, inflation, and economic uncertainty weighed on demand.

GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan says that the President Donald Trump administration’s plan to offer 40 million barrels of oil is not seeing as much interest from companies, pointing to global refining capacity woes.

Department of Energy Issues Request for Proposal

In an official statement on Tuesday, the Department of Energy issued a request for proposal, offering up to 40 million barrels of oil to companies as part of the 172-million-barrel release announced by Trump in March this year amid the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) 400-million-barrel commitment.

“Deliveries under awarded exchanges are scheduled for November and December 2026,” the statement said. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said that the move would help “stabilize oil markets” and benefit people globally as gas prices continue to surge.

“Participating companies will return the 40 million borrowed barrels with additional premium barrels, ensuring immediate market supply while increasing the SPR’s long-term inventory,” the DOE said.

The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said that over 284 million barrels of oil remain in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) as of September 18.

Patrick De Haan Weighs In

Taking to the social media platform X on Tuesday, De Haan said that while the U.S. was offering barrels, “not many buyers” were looking to accept the offer. “June RFP [Request for Proposal] only saw about half a million bought,” he said. De Haan added that oil was not “so much the challenge right now as global refining capacity.”

Oil Movement

At the time of writing this article, the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures contracts expiring in November 2026 declined slightly to $89.30. Meanwhile, Brent futures contracts maturing in November also declined 0.34% to $95.83 at the time of writing this article.

On the other hand, the United States Oil Fund (NYSE:USO) ETF was up 0.04% at $143.41 during overnight trading on Tuesday after declining 4.44% to $143.35 at market close. The ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (NYSE:UCO) ETF also gained 0.85% to $52.4 during overnight trading.

Data from the American Automobile Association (AAA) showed that the national average price of gas fell to $4.4558/gallon on Tuesday. Diesel also declined, with the national average price at $6.4391/gallon on Tuesday, compared to Monday’s national average of $6.4531/gallon.

Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) shares are trading above $1,000 ahead of its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report due after the bell on Wednesday, and a growing chorus of retail traders on social media is betting the chipmaker will finally announce a stock split as AI and high-bandwidth memory demand push the stock into rarefied territory.

Retail Traders are Buzzing About a Split

One trader asked in a post on social media platform X whether it “would make sense for $MU to perform a stock split tomorrow,” and another user warned the share price would “get annihilated” if Micron went ahead with one.

Other posts floated a 10-for-1 split, with price targets between $1,500 and $2,500 per share, while one trader predicted Micron would announce “a stock split of at least” around Q1 of 2027.

Not everyone is convinced a split changes much.

One user argued that the chipmaker “doesn’t need to double to $2,000 for the split to matter,” since “post-split options volume explodes, retail participation rises, and the float psychologically expands.”

A Reddit user pushed back on the split talk altogether, pointing out that SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ:SNDK) is trading even higher at $1,729.76 and still hasn’t split its stock.

One user predicted a split if they post earnings per share of $45.

Why Micron Stock Has Surged

Micron is one of three major memory chipmakers, along with South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY), and has been one of the best-performing stocks over the past year as a memory shortage has sent chip prices skyrocketing.

The stock’s forward price-to-earnings ratio is 6.8, compared with the industry average of 37, according to Benzinga Pro.

Mega-Cap Splitters

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) did a 10-for-1 split in 2024 when its shares traded around $1,200, while Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) split its stock four-for-one in 2020.

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) authorized a 20-for-1 split in 2022, and in the same year Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) completed its own 20-for-1 split, having also split 2-for-1 in 2014.

Wall Street Expects a Record Quarter

Analysts expect Micron to report fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $51.13 billion, up sharply from $11.31 billion a year earlier and a new company record, according to data from Benzinga Pro.

Micron has beaten revenue estimates for 12 straight quarters.

Analysts also expect earnings per share of $31.50, up from $3.03 a year ago, with the company having topped EPS estimates for 10 straight quarters.

Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) co-founder Bill Gates has pushed back against President Donald Trump and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang’s approach to AI oversight, arguing that the technology has already reached a level of risk that demands stronger safeguards.

Bill Gates Warns of AI Cyber, Bio Risks

In an interview with journalist Ezra Klein, Gates said increasingly capable AI systems could empower malicious actors to conduct sophisticated cyberattacks and potentially dangerous biological research.

Gates said AI systems are increasingly capable of identifying security vulnerabilities that humans have overlooked for years, describing the technology’s hacking capabilities as "stunning."

He also pointed to advances in AI-assisted molecular research, arguing that capabilities developed for legitimate medical purposes could have "dual use" potential.

According to Gates, capabilities that once required substantial resources and expertise could increasingly be accessible to smaller groups using advanced AI tools.

Gates Rejects AI Industry Self-Regulation

Gates challenged the argument that corporate liability and market incentives are sufficient to keep AI companies from releasing dangerous systems.

He compared AI with pharmaceuticals, aviation and automobiles, where governments have established safety requirements rather than relying solely on lawsuits after harm occurs.

"This is the most dangerous thing," Gates said, arguing that the potential consequences are too severe to depend on corporate self-policing.

He also questioned the effectiveness of safeguards built into commercial AI systems, noting that open-source models can potentially be modified to remove restrictions.

Gates Pushes Back on Huang, Trump AI Approach

Klein noted that Huang has argued that companies should not release AI products they believe are unsafe, while David Sacks and the Trump administration have backed an approach that places greater emphasis on industry responsibility.

Gates said the public and policymakers remain insufficiently aware of AI’s potential dangers. "Part of the reason I’m speaking so loudly — as loud as I can — is that you can’t rely on the industry to self-regulate here. I mean, it’s just insane."

He said governments face a choice between imposing safeguards now or waiting for a major cyberattack or biological incident to demonstrate the need for stronger controls.

Gates argued that safeguards should be required before such an event causes widespread loss of life.

Futurum Equities‘ chief market strategist Shay Boloor highlighted a branding faux pas by OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar, who mistakenly referred to OpenAI’s AI agent “Dots” as Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) “Muse.”

In an interview with CNBC on Tuesday, Friar incorrectly referred to Dots as “Muse”, causing Boloor to take a dig at the “brand differentiation.”

While explaining the advantages of Dots, Friar said OpenAI’s new Dots AI agents are designed to boost productivity and help users get more done, describing them as agents that can proactively "tap you on the shoulder."

Read Also: OpenAI Targets $30 Billion Mega-Round After Putting IPO Plans on Hold

How Muse and Dots Compare

Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent, launched earlier this month. OpenAI, on the other hand, partnered with Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) to bring its new AI agent, Dots, into the enterprise sector on Tuesday.

Notably, the two AI agents have distinct functionalities and target markets. Muse is designed to proactively assist users in managing tasks and achieving goals, operating across the apps they use daily. It can handle tasks from sending emails and booking travel to independently planning and executing complex goals, including browsing websites, filling forms, and negotiating for users. It also uses Stripe’s Link for purchases, making it the first AI agent covered by Link’s purchase protections.

On the other hand, Dots, powered by OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, is an autonomous agent aimed at corporate systems. It can connect to over 4,000 apps and continue working on several projects without user intervention. OpenAI said Dots can monitor customer feedback, develop and test fixes, submit pull requests for review, and communicate with users via ChatGPT, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) require $1 trillion in combined revenue between 2028 and 2030 to achieve a 15% return on invested capital for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

However, these companies’ existing cloud service backlogs total $1.69 trillion, covering 59% of that required revenue.

Capital Expenditure and Returns

To justify upfront capital expenditures on AI infrastructure, U.S.-Based hyperscalers must meet specific future revenue thresholds. According to a financial framework published by Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research, the path to profitability is supported by current revenue pipelines.

Summarizing the data, Futurum Equites’ Shay Boloor noted on X that “Goldman says $AMZN, $MSFT and $GOOGL only need ~$1T of 2028 to 2030 revenue to earn a 15% ROIC on AI capex.”

This $1 trillion revenue target represents the amount needed over a three-year period to hit the 15% Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) threshold.

Breaking Down the Cloud Backlogs

Financial models indicate that existing contractual commitments provide a foundation for these capital investments. The three companies reported a combined backlog of $1,687.9 billion as of the second calendar quarter of 2026.

According to the graphic shared by Boloor, Microsoft leads with a reported backlog of $678 billion, followed by Amazon at $513.9 billion, and Google at $496 billion. According to Goldman’s analysis, Microsoft would need to convert about 39.6% of its current backlog into revenue, compared with 67.7% for Amazon and 77.7% for Google, to meet their respective shares of the $1 trillion 2028-2030 revenue requirement.

Backlog figures reflect Goldman Sachs’ proprietary Calendar Quarter (CQ2’26) normalization and estimates, which may differ from reported company SEC filings.

Market Speculation and Upside

The ratio of required revenue to current backlog alters the perceived risk of ongoing data center expansions. Analysis of the Goldman Sachs data emphasizes this buffer, with Boloor saying: “That’s just ~60% of the ~$1.7T backlog already on the books, which makes AI buildout look a lot less speculative with even more upside if utilization or pricing moves higher.”

The underlying framework calculates these returns assuming 29 gigawatts of implied capacity added, factoring in utilization rates scaling to 85% by the year 2030.

Summary

Rockwell Automation delivered a strong Q3 with double-digit year-over-year growth in sales and earnings, exceeding expectations.

Q3 sales increased by 8%, with organic sales up 10%; Intelligent Devices and Software & Control segments showed significant growth.

The company highlighted strong demand in semiconductor, data center, and e-commerce/warehouse automation, while noting early project activity in automotive and life sciences.

Reported enterprise operating margin expanded to 22.3% with adjusted EPS of $3.49, representing over 20% growth year-over-year.

Former President Bill Clinton warned that abrupt changes to HIV funding could disrupt treatment and prevention programs, arguing that countries need a carefully planned transition toward greater ownership.

Clinton Warns of HIV Treatment Disruptions

On Tuesday, in a post on X, Clinton said decades of efforts had focused on lowering the cost of HIV medicines while expanding access to prevention and treatment.

"Country ownership is the goal. But a deadline isn’t a transition plan," he said.

He argued that making HIV medicines cheaper would not be enough if patients could not access them.

"Cheaper medicines mean nothing if they never reach people," Clinton said, warning against allowing treatment to be interrupted or prevention efforts to stop. "What kind of country are we if we knowingly allow treatment to be interrupted, prevention to stop, and people to be left to die?"

He also warned against reversing years of progress for political reasons.

"We should be building for the possibility of tomorrow," Clinton said. "Destroying decades of hard work to score political points carries a cost measured in human lives."

"And no perceived, short-term political victory is worth that," he added.

FDA Approved Gilead’s Bixlenvo

Last month, the FDA approved Gilead Sciences Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GILD) Bixlenvo, a once-daily single-tablet HIV treatment for adults who maintained virologic suppression.

The approval was based on Phase 3 ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2 trials, which showed the treatment maintained viral suppression at 48 weeks and was generally well tolerated.

The trials also found improved treatment satisfaction among patients switching from complex regimens, while ARTISTRY-2 showed no significant overall impact on patient weight.

Global Health Funding Concerns

On Monday, Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE:LLY) launched the Lilly Change the Course Commitment, a global health initiative aimed at expanding access to diabetes and obesity treatments in low- and middle-income countries by 2040.

The company said it would focus on clinical development, medicine registration and strengthening local health systems.

Last year, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT)  co-founder Bill Gates warned that child deaths were rising for the first time in decades as global health funding declined.

Modeling estimated that 4.8 million children under age 5 would die in 2025, up from 4.6 million in 2024, while Gates warned that reduced funding could reverse progress in preventing childhood deaths.

Medicare Advantage premiums are projected to fall 16.5% in 2027, while average premiums for standalone Medicare Part D plans are expected to rise by less than $1 per month, from $35.09 in 2026 to $36 in 2027, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services said Monday.

Premiums And Choices

CMS said the weighted average monthly Medicare Advantage premium is projected to decline from $14.37 in 2026 to $12 in 2027. For Medicare Advantage plans that include prescription drug coverage, the average monthly Part D premium is projected to fall about 38%, from $11.32 in 2026 to $7 in 2027.

More than 99% of Medicare beneficiaries are expected to have access to at least one Medicare Advantage plan in 2027, while 97% will have access to at least 10 choices. About eight in 10 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries are expected to be able to remain in their current plan with the same or a lower premium.

The announcement comes ahead of Medicare Open Enrollment, which runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7. Beneficiaries can use Medicare.gov to compare 2027 premiums, costs, benefits, and coverage options.

In the press release, CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz said, "CMS is keeping premiums stable," while urging beneficiaries to review their coverage and compare their options during Open Enrollment.

The announcement follows CMS’ July decision to end the Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration after the 2026 plan year, a move that had raised questions about potential 2027 drug-premium increases.

CMS said on Tuesday that 93% of non-low-income beneficiaries will have access to an enhanced Part D plan costing less than $6 a month in 2027.

Musk Renews Attack On Delta Wi-Fi

"Best way to sandbox an AI is to put it on a Delta flight – it will have no chance of accessing the Internet!" Musk wrote on social media platform X.

Musk’s latest jab came after he publicly predicted Bastian would "lose his job" over reported remarks attributed to the Delta CEO suggesting the airline rejected Starlink partly because it did not want to work with Musk, though Delta had not confirmed those comments.

Tuesday’s social media digs extend Musk’s criticism of Delta’s satellite strategy. On Monday, he said "Delta will lose a lot of customers" after a user contrasted the airline with United Airlines Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:UAL), which is expanding Starlink across its fleet. United said in July that Starlink was installed on 450 mainline and regional aircraft, with fleetwide coverage targeted by the end of 2027.

Earlier this year, Musk slammed Delta’s approach, saying SpaceX wanted Starlink to work without an "annoying portal," while criticizing Delta’s proposed customer experience as more cumbersome.

Delta Bets On Amazon Leo Instead

Delta chose Amazon Leo instead. The airline will begin installing Leo on 500 aircraft in 2028, integrating the high-speed, low-latency service with Delta Sync. CEO Ed Bastian called it "the fastest and most cost-effective technology available" while highlighting Delta’s existing relationship with Amazon Web Services.

Delta’s existing Wi-Fi footprint is already extensive. The airline says free Delta Sync Wi-Fi, presented by T-Mobile, reaches more than 1,200 aircraft and has logged more than 160 million customer sessions since launch. CNBC’s “Fast Money” traders debated whether Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Muse could pressure Apple Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AAPL) Services business after Bank of America warned that AI agents may increasingly transact for users without routing spending through the App Store.

Meta gained almost 30% in the last month versus Apple’s 2%.

Bank of America Flags Services Risk but Stays Bullish

Bank of America maintained its Buy rating on Apple, citing the company’s strong position in hardware and devices, but warned that AI agents could redirect some transactions away from Apple’s ecosystem.

Contributor Courtney told CNBC on Wednesday that the risk is real but questioned whether Muse will ultimately emerge as the dominant agent.

She noted that Apple is pursuing on-device AI while Muse faces growing competition from OpenAI and several other agentic AI platforms. “Is it at risk? Yeah. Is it Muse who does it? I think that’s that’s the big question,” she said.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Traders Question Near-Term App Store Impact

Another contributor questioned how much Muse could actually hurt App Store economics. He said Apple earns commissions on only a portion of App Store activity, particularly gaming and in-game purchases.

Muse is more likely to handle transactions such as food delivery and airline bookings, areas where Apple does not currently collect App Store commissions, he said.

“So, I get the thesis, but in practice, I don’t think it actually happens right now,” he said.

Muse’s Enterprise Push Adds Uncertainty

Another trader highlighted Meta’s enterprise ambitions and its recruitment of the MongoDB CEO, saying that development suggested Muse could eventually reach further into commercial activity than initially expected.

The panel broadly viewed agentic AI as a new competitive risk for Apple, but questioned how quickly Muse could materially disrupt Apple’s Services revenue or whether Meta will ultimately capture that opportunity.
